All 65 files were processed. Depth was tiered against a hard context budget — the tree is ~1.29 MB / ~320k tokens of dense normative tables, which cannot be held verbatim in one pass. Depth applied: (a) FULL text — gear-marketplace-index.md, 13.11, 13.12, 13.13, gear-marketplace-cx.md Cross-Cut Map + CX-01..CX-07 details, and every file of units 13.04, 13.07, 13.09, 13.10, 13.05, 13.08 at Decisions + Open Questions + States + Children + Role Matrix depth; (b) DECISION-SPINE — units 13.01, 13.02, 13.03, 13.06 read at Decisions + Decision Log + Open Questions + Children + Role Matrix depth (13.06 also States), with their Behavior/Edge-Case tables and Deep Think rationale not read line-by-line; (c) MACHINE-CHECKED across all 65 files with no sampling — cross-file D-/DT-/Q- citation resolution (3 hits, all judged non-substantive on review), open-question well-formedness (215 rows, 0 malformed: every row carries a non-empty owner and a non-empty deferral target), vague/untestable-normative scan over every Decisions and Decision Log row, structural compliance (index+cx presence, Role Matrix population, Role Lens/Status/Behavior/Decisions/Open Questions/Cross-Cut Notes/States/Edge-Cases presence in all 43 leaf files — zero omissions), and Children-table-to-filesystem correspondence. Residual risk is concentrated in the unread Edge-Case prose of the 16 mega-files in units 13.01/13.02/13.03/13.06; a contradiction stated only inside one of those tables and nowhere in a Decision, Open Question, State or cross-cut entry could have been missed. Dimensions 1 (Problem Clarity), 2 (Persona Specificity), 4 (Constraint Explicitness) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are marked N/A for every unit: they are owned by meta/problem-statement.md, meta/personas.md, meta/constraints.md and meta/competitive-landscape.md respectively, none of which is in this domain. Dimensions 3, 5, 7 and 8 were scored on all 11 units (44 applicable checkpoints; 2.5 points; 5.68% raw ambiguity). Structural compliance (dim 8) is clean on all 11 units. The strongest positive signal: 215 open questions all carry owner + deferral target, and constants that matter are fixed with numbers and rationale (offer expiry 48h configurable 24h–7d, 6 moves max, ≥5%/24h re-offer gate, hold durations 15min/24h/48h/72h, return label 14 days, condition assessment 72h, auto-cancel at +5d, staleness 90d/14d/30d, sold-elsewhere budget 2% of trailing-90-day orders floor 2, corroboration ≥3 listings/≥3 accounts/≥30d/≥1 sale, activation at ≥80% coverage, restocking ≤15%). No prior audit output was consulted; nothing under .memory/wiki/specs/audits/ outside run5/ was opened.

findings.claim: 13.12's storefront return-window default is defined as the buyer's statutory floor, and 13.12 D-05 forbids any undefined term from existing — but the ratified primary market has no statutory floor, and 13.12 states no fallback and carries no open question on the point. The three statements are not jointly satisfiable for a US buyer, which is the launch market.
findings.evidence: 13.12-gear-seller-storefront-policies.md:52 — "| **Return window** | integer days, `[statutory floor .. 365]` | the buyer's statutory floor (D-02) | **extend only** (D-06) | Floor resolves per **buyer's** jurisdiction, not the seller's. |"  ·  13.12-gear-seller-storefront-policies.md:194 — "| D-05 | **No seller ever trades with undefined terms.** Defaults are applied at storefront creation, inside CX-M15's activation | An unconfigured policy set is a dispute waiting. There is no null state to render. |"  ·  13.08-returns-rma-warranty/13.08-returns-rma-warranty-index.md:46 — Q-01 RESOLVED: "**Primary market: UNITED STATES to start**" and "US has no federal 14-day withdrawal right (unlike EU) — returns are policy-driven per seller"  ·  corroborated at ground truth, meta/constraints.md:267 — "| Consumer protection / returns | Physical + digital goods | **v1.5** | US has no federal 14-day withdrawal right (unlike EU) — returns are policy-driven per seller |"
findings.forcedInvention: The storefront return-window default value for a US destination. Two competent implementers reading 13.12 alone build materially different products: one resolves the absent floor to 0 days (a 'no returns' shop by default, which 13.12 DT-02 spends a whole hypothesis arguing is the dark pattern to avoid), the other resolves it to 14 days by importing the EU number the file's own examples use ("Your 7-day window is below the 14-day minimum for buyers in the EU", line 77). 13.08.01 Q-01 does track the owner call — "the owner must decide what return floor the platform itself imposes" (User → /create-prd) — but 13.12, the file that actually defines the default and forbids a null state, carries no marker pointing at it, so a reader of 13.12 has no signal that the value is undecided rather than derivable.

findings.claim: 13.10.02 D-02 fixes the turnaround buffer as "configurable" with a default described only as "conservative" — no value, no range, no unit, and no open question anywhere in the unit covering the number.
findings.evidence: 13.10-gear-rental-backline/13.10.02-rental-availability-reservation.md:79 — "| D-02 | Turnaround buffer is configurable and defaults conservative | A unit returned Monday is not rentable Monday; ignoring that guarantees the DT-02 cascade. |"  ·  restated with the same non-value at 13.10-gear-rental-backline/13.10.02-rental-availability-reservation.md:39 — "| Turnaround buffer too short | Back-to-back bookings with no time to inspect | Buffer must be configurable and default conservative |"  ·  the unit's three open questions cover other ground entirely: Q-01 (resolved — CX-M05 is the shared mechanism), Q-02 ("Can the platform re-source a replacement when a return runs late"), Q-03 ("Can escrow hold a deposit for a festival booking made 8 months ahead?") — 13.10-gear-rental-backline/13.10.02-rental-availability-reservation.md:87-89
findings.forcedInvention: The default turnaround buffer in days. "Conservative" is untestable as written and the value is buyer-visible: it directly determines which dates a renter is offered. One implementer ships 1 day (the file's own worked example is "a unit returned Monday is not rentable Monday", which implies 1), another ships 3 days to cover inspection plus a weekend. The domain sets exact constants of this kind everywhere else it matters (13.05.01 D-06 offer expiry 48h/24h–7d, 13.03.03 D-07 five named hold durations, 13.02.04 D-03 seal at label print + 15 min), and 13.12 shows the tree's own convention for a not-yet-measurable constant — ship a numbered "seed" and say so. Note 13.10 sits in the MoSCoW WONT bucket, which lowers urgency but does not resolve the value.

findings.claim: 13.10.03 D-04 states the post-return damage-assessment window is "bounded and short" with no duration anywhere in the file, while the States table promises the renter a "bounded window" it never quantifies — and the unit's open questions cover the wear/damage line and deposit shortfalls, not this clock.
findings.evidence: 13.10-gear-rental-backline/13.10.03-deposits-damage-return-condition.md:82 — "| D-04 | The assessment window is bounded and short | An open-ended window on a unit that goes out again tomorrow makes findings unattributable. |"  ·  13.10-gear-rental-backline/13.10.03-deposits-damage-return-condition.md:54 — "| Partial | Returned, assessment pending | \"Returned — checking condition\" with a bounded window, not indefinite |"  ·  the Edge Cases row gestures at a third, inconsistent magnitude at 13.10-gear-rental-backline/13.10.03-deposits-damage-return-condition.md:39 — "| Damage found after the unit is already out again | Assessment window is minutes at a loading dock, not days | Late findings are unattributable — which renter? |"  ·  open questions at :88-90 cover pooled-assignment vs per-unit history (Q-01), the wear/damage line (Q-02) and damage exceeding the deposit (Q-03) — none covers the window length
findings.forcedInvention: The assessment window duration, and its unit. The file's own three statements point in different directions — "short", "bounded", and "minutes at a loading dock, not days" — so an implementer must choose between a minutes-scale dock check and a day-scale inspection period. The renter's deposit is held for exactly this interval, so the choice is money the renter can see. The sibling mechanism in the sale flow is specified exactly (13.08.01 D-15: "Seller's condition assessment: 72h from the return's delivery scan, then accepted as-received"), which is the shape this decision needs and does not have.

findings.claim: 13.04.02 D-03 makes auto-repricing "rate-limited" without stating the rate, and the limit is the load-bearing half of the decision — DT-02 identifies an automated-agent market racing to the floor as the risk the rate limit exists to damp, so the number decides whether the mitigation works.
findings.evidence: 13.04-price-discovery-market-data/13.04.02-pricing-suggestions-repricing.md:78 — "| D-03 | Auto-repricing is opt-in, floor-bounded and rate-limited | Per DT-02. |"  ·  the risk it is answering, at 13.04-price-discovery-market-data/13.04.02-pricing-suggestions-repricing.md:60 (DT-02) — "Two Operators auto-repricing against each other on comparable stock will race toward their floors with nobody deciding anything — the well-documented retail-algorithm failure mode"  ·  and at :41 — "| Two sellers auto-repricing against each other | Race to the floor with no human in the loop | See DT-02 — a real market-structure risk, not a bug |"  ·  the file's three open questions are about market-shaping posture (Q-01), counted stock (Q-02) and paid tiering (Q-03) — 13.04-price-discovery-market-data/13.04.02-pricing-suggestions-repricing.md:85-87 — none carries the rate
findings.forcedInvention: The repricing frequency cap (and whether it is per listing, per seller or per model). This is buyer-visible product behaviour, not a tuning knob: a once-per-day cap makes a two-seller race take weeks and keeps a human in the loop, while an hourly cap lets the same race run to the floor inside a day — the exact failure DT-02 accepts the feature only because it is damped. The opt-in and floor halves of D-03 are both fully specified; only the third clause is empty.

findings.claim: 13.02.04 Q-02 rests its deferral on the claim that meta/constraints.md marks GDPR/CCPA and consumer protection as [PENDING]. That premise is false against the current tree, and the sibling index question in the same unit explicitly records it as stale — the two rows cannot both be true.
findings.evidence: 13.02-condition-originality-disclosure/13.02.04-condition-evidence-pack.md:170 — "| Q-02 | How long is a sealed pack retained? … and `meta/constraints.md` has GDPR/CCPA and consumer protection both `[PENDING]`. An agent cannot pick a retention period that is simultaneously a legal defence and a privacy commitment. | User | `/create-prd-security` |"  ·  contradicted in the same unit at 13.02-condition-originality-disclosure/13.02-condition-originality-disclosure-index.md:49 — "| Q-03 | ~~… `meta/constraints.md` flags consumer protection as `[PENDING]`.~~ **RESOLVED — not within v1/v1.5 scope, and the `[PENDING]` premise is stale.** `meta/constraints.md` § Compliance was confirmed 2026-07-18 …"  ·  ground truth confirms the index row: meta/constraints.md:261 — "| CCPA/CPRA + state privacy patchwork | All user data | **v1** | …" and meta/constraints.md:267 — "| Consumer protection / returns | Physical + digital goods | **v1.5** | …" — neither row carries a [PENDING] marker  ·  the same premise was corrected in place elsewhere in the tree, at 13.06-cart-checkout-orders/13.06.03-layaway-staged-payment.md:87 — "`meta/constraints.md` lists consumer protection as `[PENDING]` … **Narrowed, not answered**: D-32 sets the primary market to the **US** and `meta/constraints.md` now carries a consumer-protection row"
findings.forcedInvention: Nothing is forced at build time — the question is properly owned (User → /create-prd-security) and the retention durations are genuinely statutory. What the stale premise costs is the scope of the deferred decision: a reader takes Q-02 to mean the jurisdictional frame is still unset, when it is set (US-first, CCPA/CPRA at v1, consumer protection at v1.5), which is exactly the input needed to bound the retention answer. The sibling row in the same unit and the equivalent row in 13.06.03 were both updated; this one was not.
